create_refinery_n_reactors.ponder.shared: Industrial arm assembly
The industrial arm runs on rotation; the faster it turns, the faster it works. It works items lying on depots and belts.

With nothing fitted the arm works with its own claw: it sets parts, sets cores and threads wire. Its one tool is the welding torch: use it on the arm to fit it, an empty hand takes it off. Hoppers, funnels, chutes and belts can also reach the tool slot.
The parts come from the other places it takes from, such as this chest. It takes all a step needs at once, or nothing.
Put the first item of a recipe on the depot: here an iron block. The bare arm holds it still and sets a second iron block on it.

An arm with the welding torch does the next step: it draws a bead round the item that cools from white to silver. Between steps the item keeps its progress, so any arm that can do the next step goes on.
After the last step the item is the product: a welded iron beam. JEI shows every arm assembly; recipes are of type create_refinery_n_reactors:arm_assembly.

Like Create's mechanical arm, right-click blocks with the arm in hand before placing it: once marks a place to take from (blue), twice a place to put to (orange), three times unmarks it. The arm works only on the depots and belts marked to take from.
With a place to put to marked, the arm that does the last step carries the product there; otherwise it stays on the depot.

create_refinery_n_reactors.ponder.shared: Relay computer
The relay computer is the base of a multiblock.
Stack at least two relay racks, made of large relays, on top of it.
Once formed the relays start clicking, and it takes over the nearest formed reactor within 16 blocks.
Set the target output with the value panel on the front (10-100%). Right-click shows the status.
On a fission core it moves the control rods to hold that share of nominal power, backing off if fuel or coolant runs hot.
On a fusion reactor it runs the start-up: vacuum, coil cooling, magnets, then plasma, and steps output down if the blanket runs hot.
A redstone signal on the computer hands control back to the operator.
